sentences.text: The preserved snout fragment measures 221 mm in length.
This fragment features seven pairs of teeth situated entirely forward of the nasoantorbital fenestra.
Unlike neighbors from the Santana Formation, these teeth are homodont, meaning every tooth shares the same shape.
Each tooth is long, straight, and conical, reaching a maximum length of 9 mm.
The holotype specimen was acquired by the German State Museum of Natural History Karlsruhe from an illegal digger near Santana do Cariri.
David Martill formally named and described the species Unwindia trigonus in 2011.
The genus name Unwindia honors the British pterosaur expert David Unwin.
David Martill initially concluded that Unwindia was a basal ctenochasmatoid without performing a phylogenetic analysis.
Mark Witton suggested in 2013 that Unwindia might belong to the family Lonchodectidae, but Alexander Averianov argued in 2020 that it does not.
Consequently, Unwindia is classified within the superfamily Ctenochasmatoidea, with its family status listed as uncertain and possibly Lonchodectidae.
Unwindia was a pterodactyloid pterosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous period in what is now Brazil.
The holotype was recovered from the Santana Formation of the Araripe Basin, dated to the Cenomanian stage.
The estimated time range for Unwindia spans between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago.
